topic: Blue whale heart: 2 bpm on dives, surface racing, 180 kg heart, size limit
hook: Blue whale hearts can beat twice a minute
caption:
In 2018, Stanford researchers stuck a sensor on a wild blue whale in Monterey Bay. While it dove for food, its heart slowed to just 2 beats a minute. Back at the surface, it raced to 37.

The study suggests the biggest animal ever may already be pushing its heart to the limit. That could be one reason nothing alive has grown larger. Source: Goldbogen et al., PNAS 2019.

1/4 2 beats per minute (2 bpm)
Scientists suction-cupped a sensor to a wild blue whale. On deep dives, its heart dropped to just 2 beats a minute.
📷 AWeith (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

2/4 Then it races (37)
Back at the surface, it jumped to 25–37 beats a minute to reload oxygen fast, close to its maximum.

3/4 A 180 kg heart (180kg)
A blue whale heart preserved in Canada weighs about 180 kg, roughly as much as two adult men.

Researchers think its heart already works near its limits, which may help explain why no animal has grown bigger.
